title: Conditional R-078: give spin feedback direct stroke authority
hypothesis: Applying spin-error feedback directly to the periodic stroke raises slow-spin success without restoring the harmful capture compression.

prediction.against: R-078 constant-stroke-gain control on the qualified exact zero-curl parent
prediction.rationale: Beating an equally evaluated constant-gain control distinguishes useful feedback from merely strengthening the open-loop stroke. This conditionally re-triages R-078 because the first proposal supplies a prospective qualification path; its earlier deferral measured no repair outcome.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study r081_stroke_feedback --log-dir logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback"'
code_changes: New study module lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/stroke_feedback.py registered as --study r081_stroke_feedback in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py; settings in the research_protocols block of config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml. Preflight: logs/pen_spin/r080_zero_curl_qualification_90/qualification.json must say qualifies and repair_parent_eligible, else the study exits before any episode. The parent is the qualified exact zero-curl clamp (the R-065 curl_clamp substitution of config/pen_spin/r046_block3_incumbent, hashes checked).

Feedback: one audited substitution on the clamp's source, + rolling * gait becomes + self._stroke_gain(spin) * rolling * gait, with gain = clip(4 / max(|spin|, 1), 0.5, 2), spin the policy's own axial rate (5 * obj_angvel projected on the pen axis, rad/s) from the current observation, per environment per step. Constant control: the arithmetic mean of that gain over all recorded in-play steps of the clamp's archived R-068 fresh and promotion runs, frozen with provenance before any episode. Identity form returns exactly 1.0, gated bit for bit offline on D-050's archived observations. Compression stays zero; every other term unchanged.

One frozen 120-case Stage-3 manifest on seed 4663 at config/manifests/pen_spin_stage3_r081_block_s4663.yaml (cases 0-9 unused, promotion 10-39, fresh 40-119), placement-disjoint from every committed pen-spin manifest. Arms zero_curl, stroke_feedback, constant_gain, each on each panel in its own fresh process: six processes, 330 episodes, zero LLM calls.

Primary: stroke_feedback minus constant_gain fresh sustained success (80 pairs), 95% t interval; at least +0.05; supported if the mean is at least +0.05 and the lower bound is above zero; refuted if the upper bound is below +0.05; otherwise inconclusive. Adoption: strict promotion against the qualified parent on cases 10-39, fresh lower bound above zero against it, no more observed drops on either panel; no retry or panel enlargement. Reported per arm and panel: sustained success, paired success and drop differences with intervals and win/loss/tie, failure split, in-play mean |spin|, gain activity (fraction of in-play steps with gain outside [0.9, 1.1] and the mean gain), drive and per-axis executed-action saturation. If feedback activates without a success gain, R-043 takes priority. Held-out split untouched.

falsified_by: The fresh paired interval's upper bound against the constant-gain control is below +0.05. An interval including zero does not establish feedback benefit; failure to beat the qualified parent under strict promotion, or more observed drops, blocks adoption.

constant_gain.rule: arithmetic mean of clip(4 / max(|spin|, 1), 0.5, 2) over the clamp's archived in-play steps

metrics.decision_route: R-043 next: feedback activates without a success gain

controls.zero_curl: the qualified parent (D-057), each panel in its own process
controls.constant_gain: the feedback gain frozen at its arithmetic mean over 65,668 archived in-play steps of the clamp's R-068 runs (1.4081; quartiles 0.82 / 1.60 / 2.00), i.e. a stronger open-loop stroke with no feedback; frozen with provenance before any episode
controls.identity_gate: the gain substitution at gain 1.0 reproduced the clamp's actions bit for bit on all 23,484 archived D-050 observations
controls.preflight: R-080's qualification.json (qualifies, repair_parent_eligible) read before any episode

notes: Primary, predeclared (80 fresh pairs): stroke feedback minus constant gain -0.1625 [-0.271, -0.054] (22/80 vs 35/80; 4 wins, 17 losses, 59 ties): the upper bound is below +0.05 and below zero; refuted, and the feedback arm is worse than its open-loop control. Promotion: 9/30 vs 16/30 (-0.2333 [-0.422, -0.045]). Drops are equal in every arm and panel (3 of 30; 4 of 80).

Feedback activity: the gain was outside [0.9, 1.1] on 87% of in-play fresh steps (92% promotion) with mean 1.40, so the feedback was fully active; against the parent it changed nothing (-0.0125 [-0.095, +0.070] fresh, 22 vs 23). By the predeclared decision rule (feedback activates without a success gain) the route is R-043 next.

Unpredicted and not predeclared as a candidate: the constant-gain control (the stroke scaled by a fixed 1.408, no feedback) beats the qualified parent on both panels: promotion +0.1333 [+0.004, +0.262] (16 vs 12; 4 wins, 0 losses, 26 ties; drops 3 vs 3), which passes the strict promotion rule, and fresh +0.1500 [+0.049, +0.251] (35 vs 23; 15 wins, 3 losses, 62 ties; drops 4 vs 4), lower bound above zero; slow-spin tail failures 38 vs 52, in-play |spin| 4.71 vs 4.07 rad/s, off-centre 3 vs 1. Every criterion of the study's adoption rule (strict promotion on cases 10-39, fresh lower bound above zero, no more observed drops on either panel) is met by the control arm prospectively on frozen panels with no selection among candidates; the rule was declared for the feedback arm, so whether a control can be adopted as the incumbent is a triage question, recorded here rather than decided.

Reading: a stronger stroke helps and online modulation of it hurts. The gain law raises the stroke when the pen is slow (gain 2 below 2 rad/s) and cuts it when fast (0.5 above 8 rad/s); on the clamp's trajectories the mean of that law is 1.41, and applying 1.41 throughout is better than applying it where the law says. The learner's stroke amplitude was under-set (stroke_amp 0.56 of a 0.60 range is already near its bound; the gain acts on the whole rolling * gait term, i.e. also the load) and its axial-rate signal, being the thing the stroke changes within a cycle, makes a poor instantaneous gain input; a slow or per-cycle average would be the next feedback design if any, but the open-loop gain is the result to carry.

Executed-action saturation rises with the gain (5.3% parent, 8.7% feedback, 9.0% constant of components on fresh); the drive stays saturated above 0.99 on 92-96% of steps in every arm. Recorded in-play steps only.
Accounting: 330 Isaac episodes in six fresh processes, 0 LLM calls, about 4 min wall time. No deviation from the approved protocol. Final-test split untouched.

verdicts.reasoning: Predicted that spin feedback on the stroke would beat the same gain frozen at its archived mean by at least +0.05 fresh success; observed -0.163 [-0.271, -0.054] on 80 pairs (22 vs 35; 4 wins, 17 losses), upper bound below +0.05 and below zero: refuted, with the feedback fully active (87% of steps outside the identity band) and no change against the parent (-0.013 [-0.095, +0.070]); by the predeclared route, R-043 is next. The informative part is the control: the stroke scaled by a fixed 1.408 beats the qualified zero-curl parent on the promotion panel +0.133 [+0.004, +0.262] (16 vs 12; 4 wins, 0 losses), passing the strict rule, and on the fresh panel +0.150 [+0.049, +0.251] (35 vs 23; 15 wins, 3 losses), with drops equal (3 vs 3, 4 vs 4) and slow-spin failures 38 vs 52. It meets every criterion of the study's adoption rule prospectively, on frozen panels, with no selection among candidates; it was declared a control, so adopting it is a triage decision, not mine alone. Confidence 0.92: exact identity gate, frozen constant with provenance, 80 and 30 pairs, consistent direction on both panels.
verdicts.next_experiment: Two things for the next triage. (1) Whether the constant-gain controller (clamp plus stroke x 1.408) becomes the incumbent: it passed the strict promotion rule and fresh confirmation against the qualified parent with no more drops, which is exactly what the direction asks of a winner; if the advisor holds that a control cannot be adopted without a predeclared candidate run, a one-shot confirmation on a fresh panel (parent vs constant gain, 180-220 episodes) settles it. (2) R-043 per the predeclared route, now on whichever parent is current. Instantaneous spin feedback on the stroke is closed; if feedback on the stroke is tried again it should use a per-cycle or low-pass rate, not the instantaneous one.

verdicts.reasoning: The primary fresh paired_success_difference against the named constant-gain control was -0.1625, with a 95% interval of [-0.2713, -0.0537]; its upper bound is below both the predicted +0.05 threshold and zero, refuting the prediction and establishing worse success for feedback [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json]. Against the qualified parent, feedback's fresh difference was -0.0125 [-0.0955, +0.0705], which establishes no difference, and feedback failed the adoption gates [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json]. Feedback activated on 86.7% of fresh in-play steps, while observed drops were equal across arms on both panels, so lack of activation or additional observed drops does not explain away the failed prediction [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json]. Separately, constant gain beat the parent on promotion by +0.1333 [+0.0042, +0.2624] and fresh cases by +0.1500 [+0.0492, +0.2508], meeting the numerical adoption criteria, but adopting this control requires separate triage rather than relabeling the feedback prediction as supported [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json]. The results distinguish this feedback law from its constant-gain control but do not identify why online modulation performed worse [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json].
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage the existing R-043 anatomical-action-coordinate study because the predeclared trigger—activated feedback without a demonstrated success gain—is now met [logs/pen_spin/r081_stroke_feedback/summary.json].

direction: Resume Shadow Hand pen spinning from docs/SESSION_2026-10-27_PEN_SPIN_SUMMARY.md. First compare CMA-ES and random search at equal rollout budgets on the frozen R-046 controller's spin and centering parameters (config/pen_spin/r046_block3_incumbent). Compare both winners with the parent on fresh paired cases. Report sustained success, drops, and saturation. Keep final test locked. If tuning improves success without more drops, use the winner for repair. If feedback activates without improving success, prioritize R-043. Defer cold search and R-055. Require verified learner-state recovery before imitation. Use llm_pool with 16 workers and high reasoning effort. Run one protocol at a time.
